requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.fingerprints` states only observable hashing behavior, so it has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. There are no review roots, and none are needed.

I checked each clause for an alternative implementation that keeps the behavior but breaks the clause:

- **"Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and whitespace-separated words".** This fixes the digest value that callers see. A different digest, or a different encoding, would change the hash output, so it would change the behavior. Any code that produces the same SHA-256 values satisfies the clause. It names no library, type, signature or interface, and the encoding rules belong to the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`.
- **"The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version".** This is a behavior: the scheme string identifies the Rust hashing rules and their version. The text names no type or signature. The `OutlineLang::fingerprint_scheme` and `OutlineContent` signatures are prescribed by the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`, not by this subject. Cited declarations only supply context.
- **Doc comments, ordinary comments and attributes.** Doc comments participate, ordinary comments are excluded, and delimiters are excluded. Included prose is grouped as inner or outer, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word sequence. Reflowing prose keeps the hash, and changing its words changes the hash. Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash. Each of these is an input/output property of the hash, and any factoring of the code that gives the same hashes conforms.

The test evidence covers the behavioral side of these clauses, so I leave that to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The Rust fingerprint obligations are covered by tests that assert their outcomes.

- **Scheme identification.** `check` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` asserts that `Rust.fingerprint_scheme()` is `rust-structural-v1`. It also asserts that loaded contents retain that scheme through `inferred.fingerprint_scheme()`.
- **SHA-256 over structure and words.** `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` asserts that the hash is 64 hex characters. It also asserts that extra whitespace keeps the hash while `two words` versus `twowords` changes it. `prose_words_are_encoded_separately` and `string_literals_hash_as_words` check the same for `ab cd` versus `abcd`. The SHA-256 algorithm itself is a prescribed implementation choice. The tests can't check it independently, and the requirement has no observable obligation beyond the digest format and its behaviour.
- **Ordinary comments excluded.**
  - `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` changes a `// {cite}` line comment and the hash is unchanged.
  - The `/* note */` versus `/* edited */` case in `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` shows block comments are excluded too.
- **Doc comments participate.** Editing `Doc.` to `Docs.` changes the hash. `editing_a_doc_comment_word_changes_the_hash` and `reflowing_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` assert that changing a doc comment's words, or their order, changes the hash.
- **Delimiters excluded and reflow preserved.**
  - `reflowing_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` shows that `///` lines, a single line, extra spacing and blank `///` lines, and a `/** … * … */` block all hash the same.
  - `reflowing_inner_and_block_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash` shows `//!` lines equal a `/*! */` block, and that a `/** * */` block equals `///` lines.
  - Together these cover the `///`, `//!`, `/**`, `/*!` and leading `*` delimiters.
- **Inner and outer groups.** `inner_and_outer_doc_comments_hash_in_separate_groups` shows two consecutive `//!` comments hash like one comment. It also shows that moving a word between an adjacent `//!` and `///` changes the module's hash.
- **Attached attributes.** `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` changes `#[inline]` to `#[cold]` and the hash changes. `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` also checks hashes for an item with a doc comment and attribute, under reformatting and an edited body.

These tests are all marked `{test}` for the subject. I found no unmarked relevant test and no unresolved ambiguity.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
